chunks: And by this chain of narration, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Surely, God — Mighty and Majestic — has one thousand whiffs of His mercy on Friday, and He gives every servant from it as much as He wills.
So, whoever recites 'Inna anzalnahu fi laylati al-qadr' (Surah al-Qadr, 97:1) one hundred times after the Asr prayer on Friday, God gifts him those one thousand and their like.

key_terms.لَيْلَة الْقَدْر: The Night of Power — the night Quran was first revealed, celebrated in the last ten nights of Ramadan (Surah 97)
key_terms.نَفْحَة: A whiff, breath, or waft — used metaphorically for a portion or bestowal of divine mercy
key_terms.يَوْم الْجُمُعَة: Friday — the most sacred day of the week in Islamic tradition, elevated by special divine grace

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of reciting Surah al-Qadr after Asr on Friday?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) teaches that Friday is a day of special divine mercy, with God distributing one thousand portions of His mercy to servants as He wills. The Imam further specifies that reciting the opening verse of Surah al-Qadr (Surah 97) one hundred times after Asr on Friday earns the believer a doubled allotment — those thousand portions plus their equivalent. This teaching connects the sacred character of Friday with the Quranic emphasis on Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Power), encouraging persistent remembrance and recitation.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from Abi’l Hasan Musa b. Ja`far (as).
He said: Surely, Allah has one thousand whiffs of His mercy on Friday, and He gives every worshiper as much of it as He wills.
So, whoever recites inna anzalnahu fi laylatil qadr one hundred times after `Asr on Friday, Allah gifts him that one thousand and its like.
